examples.en: A police officer patrols the alley.
The security guard patrolled inside the building.

examples.ko: 밤에는 두 사람이 같이 순찰할 거예요.
examples.en: Two people will patrol together at night.
A patrolling car drove past.
We patrolled the coast and came back.
Volunteers patrol the neighborhood every night, so it is safe.

explain: '순찰하다'는 장소를 목적어로 받아서 '동네를 순찰하다'처럼 써요. '순찰을 돌다'도 많이 쓰고, 구경하며 걷는 '둘러보다'와는 달라서 경비나 단속 같은 임무가 있을 때 써요.

phrases.en: The police go on patrol every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '순찰하다'와 뜻이 같고, 장소를 목적어로 쓰지 않을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 순찰하다; it is often used when no place is named as the object.

phrases.en: The guard is patrolling the parking lot now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 순찰하는 중이라는 진행형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A progressive form that says the patrolling is happening right now.

phrases.en: A patrol car is parked at the front of the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순찰할 때 타는 경찰차를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the police car used while patrolling.

explain_en: 순찰하다 takes the place as its object, as in 동네를 순찰하다. 순찰을 돌다 is also common. Unlike 둘러보다 (look around), it implies a duty such as guarding or enforcement.

examples.en: In Hinduism, cows are treated as sacred.
People in the past regarded big trees as sacred.

examples.ko: 그 부족은 산을 신성시하면서 함부로 오르지 않아요.
examples.en: That tribe holds the mountain sacred and doesn't climb it casually.
Some fans treat celebrities as almost sacred.
In some cultures, fire is also held sacred.
If you treat tradition as too sacred, change becomes hard.

explain: '~을 신성시하다'처럼 목적어에 조사 '을/를'을 붙여 써요. 실제 종교뿐 아니라 '전통을 신성시하다'처럼 지나치게 높이 받드는 느낌으로도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: That mountain has been regarded as holy since long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-되다'를 붙이면 사람들이 그렇게 여긴다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-되다' it means people regard it as holy.

phrases.example: 마을 사람들은 그 호수를 신성하게 여겨요.
phrases.en: The villagers consider that lake sacred.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신성시하다'와 같은 뜻으로 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out way of saying the same as 신성시하다.

phrases.en: In India, many people hold cows to be holy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-는' turns the verb into a modifier for the noun that follows.
phrases.en_equiv: people who regard something as holy

explain_en: It takes an object marked with 을/를, as in '~을 신성시하다'. Besides religion, it can carry a sense of revering something excessively, as in '전통을 신성시하다'.

t90.ax: In Hinduism, cows are treated as sacred.

en: to interrogate; to examine; to inquire

examples.en: The police interrogated the suspect.
I saw a scene where a judge questions a witness.

examples.ko: 형사는 밤새 그 사람을 심문했지만 답을 못 얻었어요.
examples.en: The detective questioned him all night but got no answer.
Don't ask me questions as if you're interrogating me.
The prosecutor will question the defendant tomorrow.
My mom grilled me for telling a lie.

explain: 법적인 상황에서 캐묻는다는 뜻이라 일상에서는 농담처럼 '나를 심문하지 마'라고 쓰기도 해요. 사실을 확인하려고 계속 물을 때 장난스럽게 쓰는 거예요. 평소에 묻는 건 '묻다', '물어보다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The suspect was interrogated all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심문하다'의 반대 입장으로, 캐묻는 일을 당하는 쪽이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite viewpoint: the subject is the person being questioned.

phrases.example: 친구가 계속 물어서 '나를 심문하지 마!'라고 했어요.
phrases.en: My friend kept asking, so I said, 'Don't interrogate me!'
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 캐묻는 사람에게 장난스럽게 하는 반말 농담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful casual-speech joke to someone who keeps asking questions.

phrases.en: The police interrogated the suspect.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심문하다'와 비슷하지만 경찰이 조사할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 심문하다 but used more for police questioning.

explain_en: It is a legal-setting word, but people jokingly say 나를 심문하지 마 when someone keeps pressing them. For ordinary asking, use 묻다 or 물어보다.

en: small and weak nation; minor nation

examples.ko: 약소국의 목소리도 국제 사회에서 존중받아야 해요.
examples.en: The voices of weak nations should also be respected in the international community.
Powerful countries sometimes put pressure on weak countries.
This country was called a weak nation for a long time.

examples.ko: 약소국이라고 해서 할 말을 못 하는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being a weak nation doesn't mean it can't say what it wants to say.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 약소국이 겪은 어려움을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class we learned about the hardships weak nations went through.
Weak nations sometimes join forces and speak up together.

explain: 반대말은 '강대국'이고, 군사력이나 경제력 같은 힘이 약한 나라를 말해요. 가난한 나라를 가리키는 말과는 다르고 힘의 관계에 초점이 있어요. 국제 뉴스와 역사 수업에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I'm studying the relationship between weak and powerful nations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '강대국'과 함께 묶어서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with its opposite, 강대국.

phrases.en: We should listen to the voices of small nations too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 약한 나라의 의견을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the opinions of less powerful countries.
phrases.en_equiv: the voice of a weak nation

phrases.example: 전쟁 때문에 그 나라는 약소국이 되었어요.
phrases.en: That country became a weak nation because of war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라의 힘이 약해진 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a country becoming weaker in power.

explain_en: Its opposite is '강대국' (great power), and it refers to a country that is weak in military or economic power. It is not the same as a word for a poor country; the focus is on the balance of power. It appears often in international news and history classes.

examples.en: In an oppressive atmosphere, it's hard to speak freely.

examples.ko: 주인공이 억압적인 집안을 박차고 나가는 장면이 이 소설의 절정이에요.
examples.en: The scene where the main character storms out of the oppressive family is the climax of this novel.
The students are dissatisfied because of the oppressive rules.

examples.ko: 지나치게 억압적인 교육은 아이를 힘들게 해요.
examples.en: Overly repressive education makes children suffer.

examples.ko: 억압적인 정치에 맞서 사람들이 광장에 모였어요.
examples.en: People gathered in the square to stand against the oppressive politics.
I quit because of a boss who acted in a controlling way.

explain: 보통 '억압적인 분위기/가정/정책/체제'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 써요. 반대로 말할 때는 '자유로운', '개방적인'을 쓸 수 있어요. '억압적이다', '억압적으로'처럼도 활용돼요.

phrases.example: 억압적인 분위기 때문에 아무도 의견을 말하지 않아요.
phrases.en: No one shares their opinion because of the oppressive atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어 뒤에 '인'을 붙여 명사를 꾸미는 가장 흔한 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form: adding 인 lets it modify a noun.

phrases.en: That school's rules are too oppressive.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 어떤 것을 평가하며 끝맺는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 이다 makes it a predicate that judges something.

phrases.example: 부모님이 억압적으로 대하면 아이가 마음을 닫아요.
phrases.en: If parents treat a child in a suppressive way, the child closes their heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙이면 행동하거나 대하는 방식을 설명할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 으로 it describes the way someone acts or treats others.

explain_en: Suppressing freedom or expression of people, systems, or atmospheres (억압적인 분위기) It is usually placed before a noun, as in '억압적인 분위기', '억압적인 가정', '억압적인 정책' and '억압적인 체제'. For the opposite, you can use '자유로운' or '개방적인'. It also works in forms like '억압적이다' and '억압적으로'.

en: to suppress; to oppress; to hold down

examples.en: The dictator suppressed the people's freedom.

examples.ko: 부모가 아이의 감정을 억압하면 안 좋아요.
examples.en: It is bad when parents suppress their child's feelings.
He kept his discontent down and finally exploded.

examples.ko: 말을 못 하게 억압하는 분위기가 싫었어요.
examples.en: I disliked the atmosphere that kept people from speaking.

examples.ko: 학교가 학생의 개성을 억압한다는 비판이 있어요.
examples.en: There is criticism that the school suppresses students' individuality.

examples.ko: 자신의 마음을 억압하지 말고 솔직하게 말하세요.
examples.en: Don't suppress your feelings; speak honestly.

explain: 억압하다는 힘이나 규칙으로 남의 자유, 말, 감정을 누를 때 써요. 자기 감정을 스스로 누를 때도 쓸 수 있지만 이때는 '참다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 정치와 사회 이야기에서 많이 나오고 비판하는 뜻이 강해요.

phrases.example: 화를 억누르고 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: I held back my anger and said nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '억압하다'와 가깝고 감정을 스스로 누를 때도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 억압하다 and natural when holding down your own feelings.

phrases.en: We should help people who are being oppressed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '억압하다'의 피해를 받는 쪽에서 말하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used from the side of those who suffer 억압하다.

phrases.example: 회사가 직원의 의견을 억압하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: A company must not suppress its employees' opinions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의견, 자유, 감정처럼 말하거나 드러내는 것과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing with things people say or express, like opinions, freedom and feelings.

explain_en: Someone with power restricts another's freedom or feelings. 억압하다 is used when someone presses down another's freedom, speech or feelings by force or rules. It can also describe holding down your own feelings, but 참다 is far more natural there. It appears a lot in political and social talk and carries strong criticism.

t90.ax: The dictator suppressed the people's freedom.

examples.ko: 어선이 우리 영해를 침범했다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that a fishing boat had intruded into our territorial waters.
Territorial waters usually extend up to 12 nautical miles from the coast.

examples.ko: 외국 배가 영해에 들어오면 해경이 확인해요.
examples.en: When a foreign ship enters the territorial waters, the coast guard checks it.

examples.ko: 배가 영해 밖으로 나가면 공해라고 해요.
examples.en: When a ship goes outside the territorial waters, it's called the high seas.
The coast guard patrols the territorial waters all night.
I marked the boundary of the territorial waters on the map.

explain: 한 나라의 바다 영역을 말하고, 땅인 '영토', 하늘인 '영공'과 함께 묶어서 자주 말해요. 영해 밖의 바다는 '공해'라고 해요. 주로 뉴스나 사회 수업에서 만나는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The navy protects our territorial waters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라의 바다를 지킨다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means protecting a nation's sea and often appears in the news.

phrases.en: The plane passed through another country's airspace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 나라의 하늘 영역이고 '영해', '영토'와 함께 묶어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A country's sky area, grouped with '영해' and '영토'.

phrases.en: The ship catches fish in international waters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영해 밖의 바다를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sea outside a country's territorial waters.

explain_en: A country's own sea territory; legal and political term. It refers to a country's sea area, and is often mentioned together with '영토' (land) and '영공' (airspace). The sea beyond it is called '공해' (high seas). You mostly meet it in the news and social studies classes.

en: to be tolerated; to be pardoned

examples.en: That kind of behaviour is never tolerated.

examples.ko: 약속 시간에 늦는 건 용납되기 어려워요.
examples.en: Being late for an appointment is hard to accept.
Lies are not tolerated at school.

examples.ko: 이 정도 실수는 용납될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A mistake of this size can be tolerated.

examples.ko: 예전에는 용납됐던 일도 지금은 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: Things that used to be accepted are now a problem.
A society where discrimination is tolerated is not healthy.

explain: 용납되다는 '용납하다'의 피동 표현으로, 어떤 행동이 허용되고 받아들여질 때 써요. 대부분 '용납되지 않다'나 '용납될 수 없다'처럼 부정형으로 말해요. '허용되다'가 규칙상 가능하다는 느낌이라면 용납되다는 도덕적으로 봐줄 수 있느냐에 가까워요.

phrases.en: Violence is behavior that can't be tolerated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절대로 받아들여질 수 없다는 강한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Strongly means something can never be accepted.

phrases.en: That excuse wasn't accepted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 받아들여지지 않았던 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something that was not accepted in the past.

phrases.en: It's not an atmosphere where this kind of mistake is tolerated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긍정형은 드물고, 분위기나 사회를 말할 때 쓰는 편이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The positive form is rare and mostly used about an atmosphere or society.

explain_en: Yongnapdoeda is the passive form of 용납하다, used when an action gets allowed or accepted. It is most often used in the negative, as in 용납되지 않다 or 용납될 수 없다. 허용되다 feels like rule-based permission, while 용납되다 is closer to whether it can be excused morally.

examples.en: The media idolizes that player too much.

examples.ko: 사람을 우상화하면 잘못도 못 보게 돼요.
examples.en: If you idolize someone, you can't even see their faults.

examples.ko: 가수는 팬들이 자기를 우상화하지 않았으면 좋겠다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The singer said he hoped fans wouldn't idolize him.
I am worried that more people are idolizing politicians.
When I was little, I idolized my father.

examples.ko: 영웅을 우상화해서 가르치면 안 된다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think we shouldn't teach about heroes by idolizing them.

explain: '을/를'과 함께 써서 '누구를 우상화하다'라고 말해요. 단순히 좋아하는 것이 아니라 완벽한 사람처럼 떠받든다는 비판적인 느낌이 있어요. 반대 느낌으로는 '깎아내리다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Please don't idolize celebrities too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나치게 떠받들지 말라고 충고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to advise someone not to put a person on a pedestal.

phrases.en: That singer was idolized by fans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 그 사람을 떠받들어 신처럼 되는 입장에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This passive form says someone became idolized by others.

phrases.en: People deify that hero.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우상화하다'와 비슷하지만 신으로 만든다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 우상화하다 but with a stronger sense of making someone a god.

explain_en: It takes '을/를' as in '누구를 우상화하다'. It is not just liking someone; it has a critical sense of putting them on a pedestal as perfect. The opposite feel is '깎아내리다' (to run down).

examples.en: Those in power must listen to the voice of the people.
The responsibility of those who lead a country is heavy.

examples.ko: 위정자가 약속을 지키지 않으면 신뢰를 잃어요.
examples.en: If policymakers don't keep their promises, they lose trust.

examples.ko: 옛날 위정자들도 백성의 삶을 살폈다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that rulers in the old days also looked after the lives of their people.
This article sharply criticizes those in power.
What a statesman needs most is honesty.

explain: '정치인'은 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이고, '위정자'는 정치를 맡은 사람들을 무겁게 말하는 글말이에요. 뉴스 사설, 역사 글, 비판하는 글에서 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: The politicians held a meeting in the National Assembly today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이고, '위정자'는 더 무겁고 글말 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word; '위정자' is heavier and more literary.

phrases.en: The people are suffering because of the rulers' mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정치하는 사람들의 책임을 비판하는 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in writing that criticizes the responsibility of those in power.
phrases.en_equiv: the mistakes of those in power

phrases.en: The people want honesty from those who govern.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정치하는 사람들에게 요구하거나 기대하는 내용을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for expressing demands or expectations toward those who govern.
phrases.en_equiv: to expect of those in power

explain_en: '정치인' (politician) is the everyday word, while '위정자' is a weighty, written-style word for people who run the government. You will see it in editorials, history writing and critical essays.

t90.ax: What a statesman needs most is honesty.

en: to spread; to disseminate; to circulate

examples.en: That person spread a false rumor.

examples.ko: 친구의 사진을 허락 없이 유포하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not circulate a friend's photo without permission.
I reported the person who spreads fake news.

examples.ko: 거짓 정보를 유포한 혐의로 조사를 받고 있어요.
examples.en: He is being investigated on suspicion of spreading false information.
I don't know what the intention behind spreading the rumor was.
He apologized for circulating a post with an unclear source.

explain: 유포하다는 안 좋은 소문, 거짓 정보, 불법 자료를 퍼뜨릴 때 써서 대개 비난의 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서 소문을 퍼뜨리는 것은 '퍼뜨리다'가 자연스러워요. 좋은 뜻으로 알릴 때는 '알리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Who spread that rumor?
phrases.nuance_ko: '유포하다'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 유포하다 and more natural in speech.

phrases.example: 인터넷에 허위 정보를 유포하면 처벌받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you spread false information online, you can be punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거짓 정보, 소문, 불법 자료와 함께 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing with false information, rumors and illegal material.

phrases.example: 이 사진은 다른 사람에게 유포하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Please don't spread this photo to other people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁이나 금지를 말할 때 쓰는 존댓말 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite form used when asking someone not to do something.

explain_en: Active: someone deliberately spreads rumors or content, negative (소문을 유포하다) 유포하다 is used for spreading bad rumors, false information or illegal material, and it usually carries blame. In daily life, spreading a rumor is naturally 퍼뜨리다. To announce something in a good sense, use 알리다.

t90.ax: That person spread a false rumor.

examples.en: In the movie, the hero punishes the bad guys.
He got angry and said he would make the lying friend pay.

examples.ko: 소비자들이 불매 운동으로 그 회사를 응징했어요.
examples.en: Consumers punished the company with a boycott.

examples.ko: 잘못을 응징하기보다 이유를 들어 보려고 했어요.
examples.en: Rather than punish the mistake, I tried to hear the reason.

examples.ko: 약속을 어긴 친구를 응징하고 싶었지만 참았어요.
examples.en: I wanted to get back at the friend who broke the promise, but I held back.
The customers punished the unkind shop with their star ratings.

explain: '혼내다'가 가까운 사람을 꾸짖는 말이라면 '응징하다'는 잘못에 대해 따끔하게 갚아 준다는 느낌이 강하고 조금 무거운 말이에요. 부모가 아이를 혼낼 때는 쓰지 않아요. 주로 영화, 뉴스, 글에 나와요.

phrases.example: 나쁜 짓을 한 사람은 응징을 받아야 해요.
phrases.en: People who do bad things should be punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '응징'과 함께 벌을 받는 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the noun 응징, said from the side of the one receiving the punishment.

phrases.example: 저는 거짓말한 그 사람을 응징하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to make that liar pay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 나타내는 연결형으로, 강한 분노를 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form expressing a wish, showing strong anger.

phrases.en: The hero sharply punished the villain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따끔하게'를 붙여서 잘못을 단단히 갚아 준다는 느낌을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 따끔하게 stresses paying back a wrong sharply.

explain_en: Strong, harsh punishment of wrongdoers; justice or revenge feeling, serious tone. While '혼내다' is scolding someone close to you, '응징하다' feels heavier, like making someone pay sharply for a wrong. Parents do not use it for scolding children. It mostly appears in movies, news and writing.

t90.ax: In the movie, the hero punishes the bad guys.

examples.en: My uncle joined that party last year.

examples.ko: 정치에 관심이 생겨서 이번에 입당하려고 해요.
examples.en: I've become interested in politics, so I'm going to join a party this time.
If you join the party, you have to pay membership dues.

examples.ko: 유명 배우가 여당에 입당한다는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There's a rumor going around that a famous actor will join the ruling party.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 입당하지 않고 무소속으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: He didn't join a party and ran as an independent.
What made you decide to join the party?

explain: '정당에 입당하다'처럼 '~에'와 함께 쓰고, 정당에만 써요. 동아리나 회사, 모임에 들어갈 때는 '가입하다'를 써요. 반대말은 '탈당하다'예요.

phrases.example: 그는 입당 원서를 내고 정식 당원이 됐어요.
phrases.en: He submitted his party application and became an official member.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정당에 들어가기 위해 서류를 제출하는 절차를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes submitting the paperwork to join a political party.

phrases.en: My friend invited me to join the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '입당'을 써서 정당에 들어오라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 입당 to say someone recommends joining a party.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite (someone) to join a party

phrases.en: I haven't joined any political party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 정당에 가입하지 않은 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, stating that one is not a member of any party.

explain_en: Joining a political party, news and formal (정당에 입당하다) It is used with '~에', as in '정당에 입당하다', and only for political parties. For clubs, companies or groups, you use '가입하다' instead. The opposite is '탈당하다' (to leave a party).

examples.en: The National Assembly belongs to the legislative branch.
The legislative branch is the place that makes laws.

examples.ko: 삼권 분립은 입법부, 행정부, 사법부로 나뉘어요.
examples.en: The separation of powers is divided into legislative, executive and judicial branches.
The legislature passed a new law.
The president must respect the legislature's decisions.
A conflict arose between the legislature and the executive.

explain: 입법부는 뉴스와 사회 교과서에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '국회'라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많아요. 나라 일을 나누어 맡는 세 곳을 '입법부·행정부·사법부'라고 한꺼번에 묶어서 외워 두세요.

phrases.example: 입법부와 행정부는 서로 하는 일이 달라요.
phrases.en: The legislature and the executive branch do different jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 일을 나누어 맡는 곳을 함께 말할 때 자주 묶어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired when talking about the branches that share the work of government.

phrases.en: A country is divided into legislative, executive, and judicial branches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세 곳을 한꺼번에 말하는 표현이라서 교과서나 뉴스에서 잘 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names all three branches together; common in textbooks and news.

phrases.en: Laws are made in the National Assembly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입법부는 딱딱한 말이고, 일상에서는 '국회'라고 훨씬 많이 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 입법부 is formal; in daily life people say 국회 much more often.

explain_en: 입법부 is a word from news and social studies textbooks. In daily life people say '국회' much more often. Remember the three branches together: '입법부·행정부·사법부'.
